follow-up-email-after-meeting.0: A meeting turns into results in the follow-up email. Without one? People leave with different memories of what was agreed. With it, everyone has the same list of decisions, owners and dates in their inbox.
follow-up-email-after-meeting.1: What follows is a simple structure, 12 examples for common situations, subject lines that get opened, and guidance on timing and polite reminders for when nobody answers.
follow-up-email-after-meeting.2: Write 5 parts, in this order: a short thank-you, the purpose or context in one line, decisions, action items with owners and dates, and the next step. Under 150 words is the target. Shorter is fine.
follow-up-email-after-meeting.3: Send a follow-up email within 24 hours of the meeting, and the same day for sales and client meetings. Why the rush? The sooner you send it, the more accurately it reflects what was said, and the more likely people are to act on it.
follow-up-email-after-meeting.4: Not sure what to cover on that call? See [what is a discovery call](https://lynkk.ai/blog/what-is-a-discovery-call).
follow-up-email-after-meeting.5: Sensitive HR conversation? Follow your company's HR process and wording.
follow-up-email-after-meeting.6: Need formal minutes instead? See our [meeting minutes sample](https://lynkk.ai/blog/meeting-minutes-sample).
follow-up-email-after-meeting.7: Wait 2 to 3 business days, then reply in the same thread with 1 specific ask and a date. Most professionals stop after 2 or 3 polite reminders. After that, a short call or a message on another channel works better than more email.

follow-up-email-after-meeting.12: Name the meeting and the content in the subject line, and people know why to open it. That is what the best follow-up subject lines do. Use 1 of these 6 patterns:
follow-up-email-after-meeting.13: On its own, a vague subject like "Following up" gets skipped.
follow-up-email-after-meeting.14: Writing the email is fast. Remembering exactly what was agreed is the slow part, so take notes with decisions and actions marked during the meeting, and the email itself takes 5 minutes. Our [meeting summary template](https://lynkk.ai/blog/meeting-summary-template) uses the same structure as these emails.
follow-up-email-after-meeting.15: Want more phrasing ideas? [The Muse's follow-up email templates](https://www.themuse.com/advice/finally-5-email-templates-that-make-following-up-with-anyone-way-less-awkward) are a good companion read.
follow-up-email-after-meeting.16: Thank the attendees, restate decisions, list action items with owners and dates, and confirm the next step. Keep it short. Send it within 24 hours. Put decisions and action items in the first lines, so readers who only skim still see what they need to do and by when.
follow-up-email-after-meeting.17: Send it within 24 hours, and the same day for client and sales meetings. Why? The sooner it goes out, the more accurately it reflects what was agreed, and the more likely people are to act on the next steps while the meeting is still fresh in their minds.
follow-up-email-after-meeting.18: Name the meeting and the content, such as "Recap and next steps from today's review" or "Team sync Oct 21: decisions and actions". Specific subject lines get opened. Why? People can see the email concerns them. Avoid a bare "Following up", which is easy to ignore in a busy inbox.
follow-up-email-after-meeting.19: Wait 2 to 3 business days. Then reply in the same thread, restate the one thing you need and offer a quick call. Most professionals stop after 2 or 3 reminders. After that, switch channel, for example to a short call or a message, rather than sending another email.
